stickyComponents.text:
Proposed components (labelled on each board; added to the design system after owner approval)

- Approved by the owner, not yet in the system: SideNav, KeyValueList, FileDrop
- New for the desktop layout rules: NewOrdersStrip; StatusCard (the Right now card: system Badge, Switch, Menu and Button); DetailPanel (in-page, collapsible; editor variant and task variant for reject reasons, add category and special date); ResizableSplit (shadcn Resizable); collapsible side navigation. Usage rule for the system: on desktop web, no overlay sheets or modals for working tasks.
- Still missing from the system: Banner, EmptyState, ErrorState, Skeleton, Textarea, DateField, TimeField, ListRow, ActionBar, Disclosure, ProgressBar

Design-system issues (reported, not overridden here)

- Text tertiary #6E7C77 inside system components (Checkbox and Radio descriptions, disabled reasons, Input character count, Select empty text, timeline times): 4.36:1 on white, 4.18:1 on cream, 3.80:1 on the subtle surface. Under 4.5:1.
- The component bundle reads --type-*-size and --type-*-tracking variables that tokens.css never defines, so those texts fall back to the inherited size.
- A disabled Menu item dims its reason to about 2.3:1.
- Menu keeps its label only on icon triggers; Input drops an outside aria-describedby.
- Menu has no menuitemradio or aria-checked support: a ticked choice is shown by an aria-hidden check icon only. The boards add a visually hidden “, current” to the ticked label until Menu supports it.
- tokens.css publishes the type as font shorthands (--text-type-*), line heights and weights, but no size or tracking variables; the boards use the shorthands and keep the heading-xl tracking (-0.01em) as a literal.

stickyEditor.text:
Item editor decisions (in launch, owner decision)

- The editor is an in-page panel beside the items list: no side sheet, no modal. Opening it collapses the side navigation and the categories pane; the list stays visible and the row being edited is marked Editing. The divider resizes the two.
- Closing with unsaved changes asks inside the panel footer: Keep editing or Discard.
- Sections: Live immediately (price, prep, position, category), Options (read-only until #149), Customers see these only after review.
- A rejection points at its field and the reason links to it. Other: the reviewer’s note is the instruction. Not allowed on HalalGoes: read-only, Contact support.
- Submit stays off until something changed, with its reason. A price-only change on an item under review says Save changes.
- Photo: uploading → checking → ready. Submit is off until it’s ready.
- Drafts were dropped for 1.0: nothing is saved until you submit.
- Owner only at launch: there is no staff view.

stickyGaps.text:

- Answered on 1 October 2026: item availability and self-editing are in launch, hours can be edited while suspended (read-only once deactivated), and a 1024 × 768 landscape tablet pass is drawn.
- Can a deactivated restaurant still edit its menu? Drawn view only.

Needs API (listed once)

- the admin’s block reason and the hidden reason on each item, and on a refused change to a blocked item
- next closing, next opening, next change and last-order times on the service status
- who switched new orders off, on the service status (page loads)
- “pause until closing” (owner decision; waits for this change)
- suspension reason; confirm menu changes are refused while suspended
- item availability and item update events on the restaurant live stream
- field and matched words on a prohibited-ingredient refusal
- version checks on item edits and hours saves; when and by whom hours last changed; who submitted a change
- replaced change and last availability change on each item
- allergens declared, even when none apply
- switch a size or add-on off yourself (planned for version 2)
- special dates crossing midnight, same times meaning 24 hours, overlaps past midnight into the next day
- which rule covers midnight to 2:00 am on a closed special date after a late night
- whether customers see a special date’s reason, or a category with no approved item
- #149: withdraw a change, delete an item, category edits, bulk availability, sizes and add-ons
- the service status doesn’t reflect halal visibility or delisting
- confirm hours saves accept past special dates and whether they count toward the 90
- a reactivate operation for a deactivated restaurant
- the customer’s masked phone is hidden until acceptance (owner decision); the order payload still sends it

stickyHours.text:
Hours decisions

- Desktop 1440 × 900, no page scroll: Right now card on top; weekly hours and special dates side by side, each scrolling on its own.
- Special dates open in an in-page panel that replaces the list (list → date). Removing one confirms inside that panel.
- Saving hours that close you now, and leaving with unsaved changes, confirm in the save bar at the bottom of the weekly pane.
- Turning New orders on while order sound is off shows the sound prompt under the service status, not a dialog.
- Pause: 15, 30 or 60 minutes, or until closing (owner decision; needs the API change). Until closing replaces the rest of today (owner decision). Each names its end time.
- Suspended: hours stay editable, so they are ready when the account is reinstated; read-only once deactivated (owner decision).
- Special dates save straight away and never wait for Save hours. Saving weekly hours replaces them.
- Same opening and closing time means open 24 hours. Late hours that run into the next day’s first range are an overlap.
- Orders stop your average prep time before closing.
- The restaurant app is light only (owner decision).

stickyMenu.text:
Menu decisions

- Desktop 1440 × 900. The page never scrolls: the items grid is a LyteNyte region that scrolls on its own; panels open beside it, never over it.
- Overview → detail → more detail: categories (collapsible) → items → item details panel → editor panel. Opening a panel collapses the categories pane; the divider resizes list and panel.
- Availability is the approved Switch (owner decision). Turning it off marks the item out of stock until closing at once, then opens the length menu beside it with that choice ticked: Until closing, For 1 hour, Until you turn it back on. Escape or clicking away keeps until closing, so a missed second choice never leaves the item orderable. The switch moves when HalalGoes confirms. Back to Available is one tap.
- With no hours left today, Until closing is off with its reason and turning the switch off means For 1 hour.
- Rows are compact 44px; a row that must explain a state grows to fit its words.
- Review column is about review only: Approved, Under review, Waiting for first review, Not approved, Withdrawn. Drafts were dropped for 1.0 (owner decision).
- Hidden is set by the system; Blocked is the only admin state. The screen never sends a change to learn why an item is blocked.
- An expired or unverified certificate hides the restaurant: the status strip keeps the open badge and says customers can’t see you, with a link to the neutral banner. No field, no seal, no banner. Never red.
- Launch (owner decisions): restaurants edit their own menu, every new item and reviewed field goes through the HalalGoes review queue, and marking items out of stock is in launch. The view-only launch boards are gone.
- New orders live in a strip in the header, under the app bar, on every page (owner decision). The Kanban board and pinned New column are gone.
- Times are 12-hour everywhere (owner decision): 7:10 pm, 2:00 am.
- Desktop 1440 × 900 and landscape tablets from 1024 × 768 (owner decision): see the tablet row.

stickyStates.text:
Open-state keys (for the build)

Open = OPEN
Paused = PAUSED (until a time, or until closing once the API allows it)
Switched off = CLOSED_TOGGLE, with the server’s reason as sent. Who switched it off is known only from the live status-changed event, never inferred from missed orders
No order screen = CLOSED_OFFLINE
Outside hours = CLOSED_HOURS
No hours set = CLOSED_HOURS with no time ranges
Special date = CLOSED_HOLIDAY
Suspended = CLOSED_SUSPENDED

Precedence: suspended → offline → switched off → paused → special date → hours → open.
